subject: Private Offer: Renewal & Staggered Billing Request
messages:
From: Ellie Marks <ellie.marks@acumenhealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acumenhealth.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal request & billing schedule question

Hi Lauren,

We're getting close to renewal for our Redwood Private deployment. Procurement asked if we can split the upcoming yearly commitment into two invoices: 70% at contract signature and 30% billed 6 months later. They called this a "staggered billing" arrangement.

We currently have a Private Offer in progress (we received RI_Private_Offer_v1), and legal is asking whether that structure is supported by AWS Marketplace private offers and whether Redwood can accept the staggered billing on the commitment portion (the rest of the usage will continue as monthly metered).

Could you confirm feasibility and any additional paperwork or timeline implications? If possible, we'd love an updated private offer PDF to hand to procurement.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Ellie Marks
Head of Platform Procurement
Acumen Health

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Ellie Marks <ellie.marks@acumenhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal request & billing schedule question

Hi Ellie — thanks for the heads up and good question. Short answer: we can usually accommodate a staggered billing plan on the committed component, but there are two operational constraints to confirm: 1) AWS Marketplace private offers often require the seller (us) to provide an amended private offer for the new payment schedule, and 2) billing timelines for Marketplace invoicing can add ~5–10 business days to the first invoice issuance.

Action items from our side if you want to pursue this:
- I can produce an updated Private Offer PDF that shows the 70/30 split and the revised payment milestones (attaching a draft).
- Marissa will confirm whether any pricing guidance or credits need to be re-calculated when we split invoices.
- Priyom, can you flag if there are any constraints on Redwood's side for accepting a delayed final commitment invoice (terms/recognition/contract start dates)?

If procurement needs sign-off language calling out that the second invoice is tied to account uptime (e.g., not contingent on usage), we can add that language into the offer to avoid ambiguity.

I'll attach a draft for procurement review and loop in Samir at AWS Marketplace to confirm the private offer amendment steps.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: RE: Private Offer staggered billing - finance check

Lauren / Priyom — quick internal note before we send final version to Acumen.

- Finance: staggered invoicing is fine from a collections perspective, but we need to route the second invoice to the same billing entity and ensure terms reference the PO number. If they want the 30% contingent on usage thresholds, that creates revenue recognition and legal complications — ask procurement to confirm it's a pure timing change only.
- Legal: ensure the private offer references the same overall committed USD amount and term start date; do NOT shift the effective term start date because that would change how we count commitment usage.
- Ops: update the invoice templates we send via AWS Marketplace so DOCTYPE is "Amended Private Offer - Staggered Billing".

I'll stand by to update numbers once Lauren sends the final draft.

—Marissa
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Rao (AWS Marketplace) <samir.rao@amazon.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Ellie Marks <ellie.marks@acumenhealth.com>, procurement@acumenhealth.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private Offer: Renewal & Staggered Billing Request

Hi Lauren / Ellie,

Thanks for the note. AWS Marketplace supports amended private offers with custom payment milestones, but there are a couple of items to be aware of:

1) Private offer amendments need seller approval in the Marketplace console and then buyer acceptance. The amended offer will generate a new private offer ID; once the buyer accepts, we can issue the first invoice.
2) Staggered billing is permitted, but seller invoicing cadence must be clearly specified in the offer. The Marketplace will not split a single invoice across two bill-to entities — it must be the same billing entity.

Operational notes: expect +5 business days to provision the amended offer once we submit (console processing + internal validation). If Acumen needs the second invoice exactly 6 months later, include that milestone date in the offer (we recommend using absolute dates rather than "T+6 months" to avoid ambiguity).

Samir Rao
Strategic Marketplace Specialist, AWS Marketplace

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Ellie — attached is the updated Private Offer PDF (RI_Private_Offer_v2.pdf) that reflects the total committed amount, term (12 months starting 2027-06-01), and the 70/30 billing milestones on the committed portion. We used calendar dates for the second milestone: invoice #2 will be issued on 2027-12-01.

Key callouts:
- Total committed USD remains unchanged (no hidden credits).
- Second invoice is purely a timing change and not contingent on usage.
- AWS Marketplace will need us to submit an amended private offer via their console; Samir indicated ~5 business days for processing after we submit.

Next steps for Acumen:
1) Procurement to review attached PDF and confirm PO number and billing entity to match.
2) Once you confirm, Lauren will submit the amended private offer to AWS Marketplace and share the new private offer ID and DocuSign link.
3) Procurement signs the PO and returns signed_PO_acumen_2027.pdf.

Attaching: RI_Private_Offer_v2.pdf (draft), Acumen_PO_Draft_May2027.pdf (procurement-ready).

Thanks — happy to set 15 minutes if you want to walk the procurement team through the steps.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
